name: Clean case: clarified, sized, applied framework, concluded

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Our coffee chain wants to grow revenue. How would you approach this?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Before solving, I'd like to clarify a few things. What is the time horizon — one quarter or three years? What's the geography — only India or pan-Asia? And is the goal revenue growth or profit growth?

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Three-year horizon, India only, revenue growth.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Roughly speaking, India coffee market is around 10000 crore — that's an order of magnitude check. So we're sizing levers against that. Applied to this business: I'd look at existing-store same-store sales lift first because it's lowest risk. Specifically the answer is to analyze daypart mix. If breakfast traffic is below 30% of revenue (industry benchmark is 40%), we have a lever. Sanity check: 10% lift in same-store sales from a daypart program would yield about 50 lakh per store per year, that seems reasonable.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: My recommendation is to launch a breakfast SKU program in the top 200 stores within 6 months, target 25% revenue uplift on those stores, and only after that consider new-store expansion. The bottom line is: optimize first, expand second.
